reader.requirement: At COBOL-85, when SPECIAL-NAMES has DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, NUMVAL-C must read argument-1 with the comma as the decimal separator and the period as the grouping separator, in both argument formats (leading or trailing sign, CR/DB), with or without a currency string, for literal, item, reference-modified and group arguments; without the clause the roles stay as written.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.NumvalCCurrencyContentRules (inactive at 85: argument-2 content unscreened, CurrencyContentUnrestricted) and the 2002 ANYCASE/LOCALE construct gates; neither touches the comma/period roles

reader.edition-search: the comma mode is CommaFlag = ctx.Data.Configuration.DecimalPointIsComma with no edition test; grep Edition|DialectBehavior in NvScan/NumvalCDec: only the contentUnrestricted parameter (argument-2 content), not the separator swap
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for this rule: the separator swap is the same code at 85 and 2023; the 85 arm differs only in skipping the 2002 currency-content screen
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf41_04 covers literals, a leading cs, a trailing minus and a bare ,5; not CR/DB, an explicit argument-2, a reference-modified or group argument, a period-grouped value without a comma, or the clause-absent arm

probes.expected: CURRENCY SIGN '#' with DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA: '#1.234,5' = 1234.5, '# 0,01-' = -.01

probes.printed: COBOL0900 the ANYCASE keyword ... requires COBOL-2002; COBOL0900 the LOCALE keyword ... requires COBOL-2002

citations.check: OK  §1989:A.2.30.3 AR2  (2.30.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR2

reader.notes: One scan (NvScan) swaps the decimal and grouping characters from the program's DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA flag; every probed form under the clause and the clause-absent arm return the represented value. The edition is consulted on this path only for 2002 additions (ANYCASE, LOCALE, argument-2 content), none of which changes the separator roles.

refuter.evidence: Attacked the one path CommaFlag (ctx.Data.Configuration.DecimalPointIsComma) for programs whose comma mode is not written in their own SPECIAL-NAMES. §1985:VI.4.2: a contained program has no Configuration Section and the containing program's entries apply to it. Probe nest_nc.cob (outer DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA + CURRENCY SIGN '#', contained program with no ENVIRONMENT DIVISION): O1 1234.50, I1 '#1.234,5'=1234.50, I2 item '# 9.876,5'=9876.50, I3 '1,5'=1.50: MATCH. Probe sep_nc.cob (separately compiled SEPA with the clause, SEPB without, in one source): A1 1234.50, B1 '$1,234.5'=1234.50, B2 '1.5'=1.50: MATCH, so the clause does not leak to a sibling program. cite.py: 'OK  §1989:A.2.30.3 AR2  (2.30.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR2'; 'OK  §1985:VI.4.2  (4.2 CONFIGURATION SECTION)  the text is in the clause'.
